posts.author: Lionbarrel
posts.body:
I tend to enjoy deep diving into the - History?? Of Rpgmaker in between my
job hunting
and overthrowing unfinished projects. Love how older sprites used to look in alights especially are interesting. Of course, with their limited file size, they would have to be super creative back then. And just how unapologetically janky some of the sprites were are just super charming!!
Today I wanted to talk about one of my favorite ones. Chimes Quest!!
Not my screenshot*
​
"
...was an RPG development software for PC-9801 by TAKERU. It was distributed through TAKERU vending machines that provided everything from the development software to Falcom sprite editors to Sorcerian bonus scenarios on floppy disk.
"
From
conparkforever
on tumblr
Like I said, I adore the color palette and just how they were able to portray shadowing back then was also impressive to me. If you go out there, you can find the spritesheets of the Tilesets and character sprites...
Not my screenshots*
​
I've also noticed that it looks awfully familiar; They must have hired the same artist or sprite artist// as RPGMaker '97, '97+ and '98. Besides, despite being a little taller, the tiles and enemies look the same, and I'm pretty sure they're using one of the same angels as well. The art is stunning. And I wish when they make console versions of RPG Maker that they'll allow the people to customize their sprites similar to Chimes quest {They weren't the only one and strangely enough slightly recent like late 90s console games were able to edit the sprites themselves}...
For those who could be possibly wondering, no, the actors of the defaults don't have names. And even some of the character sheet actors/NPCs don't have face sprites. Only like three of the heroes do.
Which let me say, the wizard is an old man that kind of looks like Santa Claus, you don't see that in the newer gen/generations...
I have a couple of my personal projects that tries to introduce the borders and the UIs of these older games to introduce their characters in my long,
foreboding,
head cannon/Crossover/Mess of a game... As you can tell from all my successful uploads, it has been going very well.
Not my assets rip*
These are comparisons of the different sprites of Chime and '97*
​
If you guys had any older generations that you liked, feel free to drop down.So do you connect all the games in some kind of long time line like I do, or do you just kind of treat them as their own universes?
